title: feat(issue-authoring): close the gap where documented roadmap-child drafting never produces Candidate files
body:
# feat(issue-authoring): close the gap where documented roadmap-child drafting never produces ## Candidate files

## Background

`issue-authoring`'s own "Example roadmap package" child-issue template
(the shape used for every parallel-eligible roadmap child) never
mentions `## Candidate files`, and the "Required draft content" list
for roadmap children doesn't include it either — so a roadmap authored
strictly through the documented flow ships children whose
`## Candidate files` section is always absent.
`discover-shared-file-overlap` deliberately returns `[]` when that
section is missing (a designed fallback, not a bug in the parser
itself), so `candidateFiles` and `overlapFlag` come back empty/false
for every such candidate regardless of real file contention — the A4
Step 2 high-contention shared-file check becomes a structural no-op for
the common case.

Closed issue `#2237` already documented the section's parse *format*,
but that only helps once an authoring session independently decides to
add the section; it did not change what the documented drafting flow
actually generates.

## Proposed change

Pick (or combine) one of:

- (a) require `## Candidate files` in the roadmap-child "Required draft
  content" list and the "Example roadmap package" template, at least
  for children expected to run under parallel/autonomous claiming, or
- (b) have `discover-shared-file-overlap`'s own docs and/or the
  Discover-phase instructions state loudly (not just in an internal
  docstring) that the gate is a structural no-op unless the section is
  independently populated.

This matters because the roadmap authoring flow is the primary way
concurrent-claim-eligible children get created, and the overlap gate
exists specifically to protect that concurrency — silently no-opping it
defeats its purpose without any signal to the adopter that it never
engaged.

## Acceptance criteria

- Either the roadmap-child template/required-content list now includes
  `## Candidate files`, or the Discover-phase docs explicitly state the
  no-op condition where the section is absent (or both).
- `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` passes.
- If code changes are made to `discover-shared-file-overlap`, existing
  tests continue to pass and a test covers the documented behavior.

## Candidate files

- `skills/issue-authoring/references/contract.md`
- `skills/issue-authoring/references/draft-patterns.md`
- `docs/idd-helper-scripts.md`

---

_Autopilot suitability: 4 / 5 -- higher is more autopilot-suitable;
below the configured floor is human-oriented._
